first.rationale: The immediate competitive threat is concentrated in price-sensitive SMB accounts, where targeted promotional pricing previously improved both acquisition and revenue. I will verify the prior pricing experiment’s qualification, retention, and margin effects before committing, while also checking whether the onboarding result offers a stronger sustainable-revenue alternative given the current completion decline.

mid.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% decline in completion and has verified evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and a 3% improvement in 30-day retention—better aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing. The verified discount result raises a material downstream retention risk, so it should not be used this cycle.

final2.rationale: Keep the shortened-onboarding experiment. The deeper price cut increases urgency, but the only directly verified pricing evidence shows a 12% 30-day retention decline and explicitly advises against treating discounting as sustainable growth. Shortened onboarding directly addresses the completion decline and has verified gains in completion, time-to-value, and retention. The competitive churn risk remains material and should be monitored, but it does not justify an unvalidated retention-damaging discount response under the long-term qualified-revenue objective.
